operator_io_quirks: loan.branch_ID declared varchar(3) but FK to bank.branch_ID (INT) and storage is text '1','2','3' — FK child/parent declared types disagree; TS draws parent values (ints) into a String-typed child column.

loan.cust_ID FK parent column spelled 'Cust_ID' in pragma but column is 'cust_ID' — case-insensitive parent lookup required; upstream upper-cases columns so it matches, but original-spelling compare must use .lower().
loan.cust_ID has only 2 distinct values over 3 rows (1,3) — FK parent (customer) has 3 rows; child FK values are a subset, not a bijection.
acc_type declared char(1) but samples are 'saving'/'checking' (7-8 chars) — storage class text contradicts declared length; sqlite does not enforce char(1).
credit_score samples 30,20,210 — implausible as a credit score (0-850 range not enforced); no CHECK constraint.
acc_bal sample 800000 vs 2000/1000 — wide numeric spread, no range constraint.
All tables tiny (bank=4, customer=3, loan=3 rows) — TS size chooser (30..2500) will massively over-generate vs original; original_values lists are length <=4.
No NOT NULL anywhere (notnull=0 on every column incl. PKs) — sqlite PK still implies uniqueness but not null; TS may insert NULL PKs which sqlite rejects at insert (skipped).
No CHECK constraints, no UNIQUE indexes beyond PKs — drop_unique_duplicates only acts on PKs here.
All PKs are single-column (branch_ID, cust_ID, loan_ID) — composite-PK path unused; PK columns are int or varchar(3) with tiny distinct sets.
varchar(3) PKs (cust_ID, loan_ID) hold '1','2','3' — String fuzzer with length range from elements (len 1) will produce short strings; collisions likely, PK dedup will drop many rows.
Table names all lowercase, no spaces — mixed-case/spaced-name path not exercised by this DB.
operator_ts_expectations: bank.branch_ID (INT, PK): Number fuzzer, scale from 'int' -> is_int, range [-10^0,10^0] perturbed +-1/+-2; PK -> max_l0=inf so mostly fresh ints; will produce values far outside {1,2,3}.
customer.branch_ID (INT, FK): filled from bank.branch_ID final values with replacement — consistent but bank has only ~30-2500 generated rows so many duplicates.

loan.branch_ID (varchar(3), FK): String-typed child filled from bank.branch_ID (ints) — values become ints stored in text column; joins on branch_ID still work numerically in sqlite but type affinity differs from original.
loan.cust_ID (varchar(3), FK): filled from customer.cust_ID final values; customer PK dedup may shrink customer below requested size, so loan FK draws from a small set.

String columns (bname, city, state, cust_name, loan_type, acc_type): String fuzzer, length range from 5 sampled originals + pool literals; fresh strings over a-zA-Z 0-9() with 50% contaminate — implausible names/cities (FN source for queries filtering on real city/state names).
acc_type char(1): String fuzzer length range from elements 'saving'/'checking' (len 6-8) — will NOT produce 1-char values; queries expecting 'S'/'C' or length-1 will miss.

Number columns (no_of_customers, acc_bal, no_of_loans, credit_score, amount): Number fuzzer full range [-1,1] for int scale 0 perturbed — will produce 0,1,-1,2 etc., not realistic magnitudes (2000, 800000) — FN for range predicates like acc_bal>1000.
Date/Time/Bool/Bit fuzzers unused — no such declared types.

PK dedup (sample_fresh_primary_keys) on tiny varchar(3) PKs: String fuzzer over ~62-char alphabet length 1-3 gives limited space; many duplicate PKs dropped, final table sizes may be far below chosen size.
No unique non-PK columns -> drop_unique_duplicates is a no-op.

FK consistency holds (parent generated before child via table_order bank->customer->loan) so referential joins return rows; but loan.branch_ID text vs bank.branch_ID int may cause type-mismatch in strict comparisons (sqlite coerces, usually fine).

Known miss drivers: implausible numeric magnitudes and random strings (FN on value predicates); missing ties/duplicates because PK dedup and small distinct sets (FP on GROUP BY / DISTINCT / COUNT comparisons).
